tools.name: format_json
tools.description: Validate and pretty-print a string that is ALREADY valid JSON. Strict by design — it is a validity gate: valid JSON comes back formatted, anything else is rejected with the exact parse error. It never repairs, completes, or guesses. NOT for: plain text or prose (will fail), JSON embedded in markdown/prose (use extract_json_from_text first), JS objects (JSON.stringify them first), YAML (use yaml_to_json).

params.name: input
params.description: A raw JSON string, e.g. '{"key":"value"}'. Must already parse as JSON — plain text or truncated JSON is rejected, not repaired.

tools.name: generate_uuid
tools.description: Generate one or more cryptographically random UUID v4 identifiers. Use this when you need unique IDs for test fixtures, database records, session tokens, or any scenario requiring a guaranteed-unique string. Returns up to 100 UUIDs in one call.

params.name: count
params.description: Number of UUIDs to generate (1–100, default: 1)

tools.name: hash_text
tools.description: Compute a cryptographic hash of a text string. Use when you need to verify data integrity, generate content fingerprints, hash passwords (prefer SHA-256+), or produce a fixed-length digest of any input. Supports SHA-256 (default), SHA-512, SHA-1, and MD5.

params.name: algorithm
params.description: Hash algorithm: sha256 (default), sha512, sha1, md5

tools.name: count_tokens
tools.description: Estimate the token count of a text string using the cl100k_base approximation (~4 chars/token). Call this BEFORE sending any text to an LLM API to check if it fits within the model context window and to estimate cost. Returns token estimate, character count, and word count.

tools.name: base64_encode
tools.description: Encode a UTF-8 string to Base64. Use when you need to embed binary data, multi-line text, or special characters safely inside JSON fields, HTTP headers, or data URIs.

tools.name: base64_decode
tools.description: Decode a Base64 string back to UTF-8 text. Use for inspecting Base64-encoded API responses, JWT payload claims, config file values, or attachment data.

tools.name: url_encode
tools.description: Percent-encode a string for safe use in URLs. Call this before programmatically building query strings, path segments, or form-encoded bodies to prevent injection and malformed URLs.

tools.name: url_decode
tools.description: Decode a percent-encoded URL string back to plain text. Use when parsing query parameters from raw URLs or when displaying encoded values to users.

tools.name: generate_slug
tools.description: Convert any string into a URL-friendly slug: lowercase, ASCII-normalized (é→e), special characters removed, spaces replaced with hyphens. Use for generating SEO-friendly URL paths, file names, or identifier keys from user-provided titles or labels.

tools.name: validate_email
tools.description: Validate an email address against RFC 5322 syntax before storing it, sending a transactional email, or adding it to a mailing list. Returns { valid, email } — use this to avoid bounces and malformed data.

tools.name: minify_js
tools.description: Minify a JavaScript snippet, function, class, or module up to 50 KB using Terser. Returns minified code and byte savings. Use when embedding scripts in HTML templates, report payloads, or injecting inline code programmatically.

tools.name: decode_jwt
tools.description: Decode a JWT (JSON Web Token) and return its header and payload without verifying the signature. Also reports whether the token is expired and the exact expiry date. Use to inspect claims (sub, iss, exp, roles) during debugging or when integrating with an auth provider.

tools.name: text_stats
tools.description: Compute comprehensive statistics for any text: character count (with and without spaces), word count, line count, sentence count, paragraph count, and estimated reading time in minutes. Use for validating form field lengths, evaluating LLM output verbosity, or content auditing.

tools.name: generate_password
tools.description: Generate a cryptographically secure random password using crypto.randomBytes. Configurable length (4–128), uppercase letters, digits, and symbols. Use when resetting user passwords, seeding test accounts, or generating API secrets.

tools.name: parse_csv
tools.description: Parse a CSV string into a JSON array of objects (or raw arrays). Handles RFC 4180 quoted fields, escaped quotes, and custom delimiters. Use when processing spreadsheet exports, data imports, or structured text pipelines where the source is CSV. Supports up to 200 KB.

params.name: header
params.description: Treat the first row as headers (default: true)

tools.name: color_convert
tools.description: Convert a color between HEX, RGB, and HSL formats. Use when translating design tokens between CSS notations, verifying color accessibility, or normalizing color values from user input. Accepts #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(r,g,b), or hsl(h,s%,l%).

tools.name: regex_test
tools.description: Test a regular expression pattern against an input string and return all matches with their index positions and named capture groups. Use for validating user inputs, extracting structured data from text, or debugging regex patterns. Supports flags g, i, m, s, u, y.

params.name: flags
params.description: Regex flags: g (global), i (case-insensitive), m (multiline), s (dotAll) — default: ""

params.name: input
params.description: The string to test against (max 50 KB)

tools.name: lorem_ipsum
tools.description: Generate Lorem Ipsum placeholder text for UI mockups, design prototypes, or test data population. Configurable paragraphs (1–10), sentences per paragraph (1–20), and approximate words per sentence (3–30).

params.name: paragraphs
params.description: Number of paragraphs to generate (1–10, default: 1)

tools.name: timestamp_convert
tools.description: Convert between Unix timestamps (seconds or milliseconds) and ISO-8601 / UTC date strings. Auto-detects epoch vs. millisecond format. Omit input to get the current time. Returns iso, unix_s, unix_ms, utc, date, and time fields.

params.name: input
params.description: Unix timestamp (number, seconds or ms) or ISO date string. Omit to get the current time.

tools.name: diff_text
tools.description: Compute a unified line-by-line diff between two text strings (LCS algorithm). Returns added/removed/unchanged line counts and formatted diff hunks with configurable context lines (0–20). Use to compare versions of prompts, configs, code snippets, or any text where you need to see exactly what changed.

params.name: context
params.description: Context lines around each change (0–20, default: 3)

tools.name: truncate_to_tokens
tools.description: Truncate text to at most N tokens (cl100k_base: ~4 chars/token) to avoid exceeding an LLM context window. Optionally keeps the end of the text instead of the start (useful for keeping recent conversation history). Reports whether truncation occurred and the estimated token count.

params.name: from_end
params.description: Keep the end of the text instead of the start (default: false)

params.name: max_tokens
params.description: Maximum number of tokens to keep

tools.name: split_chunks
tools.description: Split text into chunks of at most N tokens (cl100k_base: ~4 chars/token) with optional overlap. Designed for RAG ingestion pipelines.

tools.name: extract_json_from_text
tools.description: Extract the first valid JSON object or array embedded in chaotic LLM output (surrounded by markdown fences, prose, or explanatory text). Handles ```json blocks and inline JSON. Call this whenever an LLM returns structured data mixed with explanation text instead of raw JSON.

params.name: input
params.description: Raw text (e.g., LLM output) that may contain a JSON object or array

tools.name: strip_markdown
tools.description: Strip all Markdown formatting (headers, bold, italic, code fences, links, lists) from text and return clean plain text. Run this before injecting scraped documentation, README files, or user content into an LLM prompt to eliminate redundant markup tokens and reduce cost.

params.name: input
params.description: Markdown text to convert to plain text

tools.name: estimate_llm_cost
tools.description: Estimate the API cost in USD for a given model and token counts. Supports all major 2024–2026 models: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o3, o4-mini, Claude Opus 4, Claude Sonnet 4/4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek V3/R1, Grok 3, and legacy models.

tools.name: escape_html
tools.description: Escape HTML special characters (&, <, >, ", ') to their safe HTML entities. ALWAYS call this before inserting any user-provided or LLM-generated content into an HTML template to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

tools.name: unescape_html
tools.description: Convert HTML entities (&, <, >, ", ', and numeric &#NNN;) back to plain characters. Use when processing HTML-encoded text from APIs, email content, or legacy database fields before passing to an LLM or displaying to users.

tools.name: fetch_veille_feed
tools.description: Fetch the latest QA & AI/LLM articles aggregated from curated RSS sources (Google Testing Blog, DEV.to Testing/QA/AI/LLM/Agents, Hugging Face Blog, Simon Willison). Perfect for agents monitoring the QA & AI landscape.

tools.name: score_geo_signals
tools.description: Analyze a webpage <head> HTML (or full HTML) for GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) signals. Returns a score /60 with per-check results and improvement tips. GEO = optimizing pages for AI-powered search engines (ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, etc.).

params.name: head_html
params.description: Raw HTML of the <head> section (or full page HTML) to analyze

tools.name: extract_json_path
tools.description: Extract a value from a JSON string using dot-notation path (e.g., "user.address.city", "items.0.name", "meta.tags"). Supports array index access via numeric path segments.

params.name: input
params.description: The JSON to traverse — a JSON string, or the object/array itself.

tools.name: generate_json_ld
tools.description: Generate a ready-to-paste <script type="application/ld+json"> snippet for GEO / structured data optimization. Supported types: WebSite, FAQPage, Article, Person, Organization, SoftwareApplication, HowTo.

params.name: fields
params.description: Schema fields as key-value pairs (name, url, description, author, datePublished, etc.)

params.name: faq_items
params.description: For FAQPage/HowTo: array of { question, answer } objects

tools.name: analyze_diff_bugs
tools.description: Pattern-based diff linter: flags a fixed set of risky shapes in changed code — query-string interpolation (SQL/Cypher/Mongo injection shape), shell interpolation, eval/new Function, empty catch blocks, regex built from a variable, fewer catch blocks than before, and named authorization guards that disappeared. Every finding cites the line that produced it. It does NOT do data-flow analysis: it cannot follow a value to a sink, across functions or files, and an empty result is not a safety verdict

params.name: context
params.description: Optional PR title or feature context for better analysis

params.name: version1
params.description: Original code (before changes). If omitted, only the new version is analysed.

tools.name: generate_test_cases
tools.description: Generate a set of test cases (valid, edge, invalid) for a given feature description. Returns test matrix with Gherkin scenarios ready to use.

params.name: inputs
params.description: Optional: list of input parameters (one per line, e.g. "email: string [required]")

params.name: feature
params.description: Feature or function to test. Be specific: describe inputs, expected behaviour, context.

tools.name: run_pr_gate_pipeline
tools.description: Review triage for a pull request. Takes a unified git diff (`git diff HEAD`) and returns: diff-lint findings with the lines that produced them, regression impact areas, a risk score 0–100 with the factors that built it (churn, files touched, sensitive paths, whether any test file changed, lint severities), generated test cases, and a PASS / CONDITIONAL / BLOCK recommendation. Advisory: the score measures properties of the diff, not the correctness of the change — it does not read the code semant

params.name: context
params.description: Optional PR title or description for richer analysis

params.name: git_diff
params.description: Unified git diff (output of `git diff HEAD` or copied from GitHub diff view)

tools.name: validate_mcp_response
tools.description: Validate that an MCP tool response conforms to expected format, schema, and content rules. Use this to QA-test any MCP server tool. Supply the tool's actual JSON result and a set of checks to perform.

params.name: response
params.description: The MCP tool result as a JSON string to validate

params.name: min_items
params.description: If response is an array, minimum number of items expected

params.name: required_keys
params.description: Comma-separated list of keys that MUST exist in the response (dot-notation for nested: "data.id, data.name")

params.name: actual_latency
params.description: Actual measured latency in ms (from the call)

params.name: forbidden_keys
params.description: Comma-separated list of keys that MUST NOT exist (e.g. "password, secret, token")

params.name: max_size_bytes
params.description: Maximum acceptable response size in bytes

params.name: max_response_ms
params.description: Maximum acceptable latency in ms (will be compared if provided)

tools.name: llm_output_validator
tools.description: Validate an LLM response against QA criteria: format checks (JSON, code, markdown), content rules (must-include, must-not-include), length constraints, language detection, and safety patterns. Essential for QA testing LLM-powered features.

params.name: output
params.description: The LLM output text to validate

params.name: max_length
params.description: Maximum character length for the output

params.name: min_length
params.description: Minimum character length for the output

params.name: check_safety
params.description: Check for PII patterns (emails, phones, SSN), profanity signals, and prompt leakage

params.name: must_include
params.description: Comma-separated strings that MUST appear in the output

params.name: must_not_include
params.description: Comma-separated strings that must NOT appear (e.g. "TODO, FIXME, undefined, NaN")

params.name: check_json_schema
params.description: If expected_format is JSON, provide required keys as comma-separated list to validate the structure

params.name: expected_language
params.description: Expected language of the output (en, fr, es, de…). Checks for common words.

tools.name: compare_responses
tools.description: Compare two ALREADY-PRODUCED outputs (e.g. model A vs model B on the same task) side by side. Returns deterministic metrics (token cosine, ROUGE-L, Jaccard, length/structure deltas, JSON diff) and a verdict. If a `reference` (ground truth) is given, scores each output against it and picks the closer one. If `model` + `api_key` are given, an LLM judge also picks a qualitative winner for the task. No re-execution — you bring the outputs.

params.name: task
params.description: The task/prompt both outputs were answering — used by the LLM judge for context

params.name: model
params.description: Optional judge model id (BYOK). When set with api_key, an LLM judge picks a qualitative winner.

params.name: api_key
params.description: Optional API key for the judge model (BYOK). Used only for the judge call; never stored.

params.name: reference
params.description: Optional ground-truth / expected answer. If set, each output is scored against it and the closer one wins (deterministic).

params.name: check_json
params.description: Try to parse as JSON and compare structurally (keys, types, values)

tools.name: analyze_responses
tools.description: Semantically analyze N already-produced model outputs for the SAME task (the MCP counterpart to the LLM Sandbox). Without a reference: computes consensus — pairwise cosine agreement, the most-representative output, and the outlier. With a `reference` (ground truth): also ranks every output by closeness (token cosine + ROUGE-L composite) and names the closest. Deterministic, no LLM, no key — gate-able in CI. You bring the outputs (2+). For a 2-way head-to-head with structural JSON diff use compar

params.name: reference
params.description: Optional ground-truth answer. If set, each output is also ranked by closeness to it and the closest one is named.

params.name: responses
params.description: The outputs to analyze (same task, N models/prompts/versions). Each item is a plain string or { "label": "GPT-4o", "text": "..." }. At least 2 required.

tools.name: prompt_test_suite
tools.description: Define a test suite for a prompt: provide the system prompt, user prompt, and expected output criteria. Returns a test plan with scored rubric — use this as input for manual or automated LLM evaluation.

params.name: max_tokens
params.description: Max token budget for the test

params.name: check_safety
params.description: Include safety/PII checks in the rubric

params.name: expected_behavior
params.description: Description of what the LLM should do (free text)

params.name: adversarial_prompts
params.description: Auto-generate adversarial test variants (jailbreak, injection, edge cases)

tools.name: mcp_server_health_check
tools.description: Generate a health check report for an MCP server's tool manifest. Validates tool definitions, schema quality, naming conventions, and documentation completeness. Paste the server manifest JSON to audit.

params.name: strict
params.description: Enable strict mode: also check for optional best practices (examples, default values, descriptions > 20 chars)

params.name: manifest
params.description: MCP server manifest JSON (the response from GET /mcp or tools/list)

tools.name: mcp_server_evaluate
tools.description: Run a full compliance evaluation against a live MCP server URL. Tests: server reachability (ping), manifest discovery (GET /mcp), schema quality (snake_case names, descriptions, inputSchema), JSON-RPC 2.0 test call, and P50/P95 latency. Returns a PASS/FIX/BLOCK verdict with a 0-100 score and per-check details.

params.name: url
params.description: Base URL of the MCP server (e.g. https://ia-qa.com or http://localhost:3001)

params.name: test_tool_name
params.description: Specific tool name to use in the JSON-RPC test call (defaults to the first tool in the manifest)

tools.name: json_schema_validate
tools.description: Validate a JSON value against a JSON Schema (draft-07 subset). Supports type, required, properties, items, enum, const, pattern, format (email/uri/date), minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, minItems/maxItems, uniqueItems, additionalProperties, anyOf, allOf, oneOf. Returns all validation errors with dot-notation paths.

params.name: value
params.description: The JSON value to validate — a JSON string, or the value itself.

params.name: schema
params.description: The JSON Schema — a JSON string, or the schema object itself.

tools.name: flatten_json
tools.description: Flatten a nested JSON object to single-level dot-notation keys (e.g. {"a":{"b":1}} → {"a.b":1}), or unflatten dot-notation keys back to a nested object. Supports custom separators.

params.name: input
params.description: The JSON to flatten or unflatten — a JSON string, or the object itself.

tools.name: xml_to_json
tools.description: Convert an XML string to a JSON object. Supports attributes, nested elements, arrays, CDATA, and namespaces. Options: parse numbers, parse booleans, ignore attributes.

tools.name: redact_pii
tools.description: Automatically detect and redact Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from text. Replaces emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit cards, IP addresses, and JWT tokens with [REDACTED_TYPE] placeholders. Safe to use before logging or sending to an LLM.

params.name: types
params.description: Comma-separated types to redact (default: all). Options: email, phone, ssn, credit_card, ip_address, jwt

tools.name: mock_from_schema
tools.description: Generate realistic mock data from a JSON Schema. Supports all common types (string, number, integer, boolean, array, object, null), format hints (email, date, date-time, uri, uuid), enum, const, and nested schemas. Perfect for testing MCP tools with realistic data.

params.name: seed
params.description: Optional seed string for deterministic output (uses first char codes)

params.name: count
params.description: Number of mock objects to generate (default: 1, max: 20)

params.name: schema
params.description: The JSON Schema to generate from — a JSON string, or the schema object itself.

tools.name: transform_json_array
tools.description: Transform a JSON array using common operations: pluck (extract specific fields), filter (by field value), sort_by (field), group_by (field), count_by (field), uniq_by (field). Useful for processing MCP tool results and LLM structured outputs.

params.name: n
params.description: For first_n / last_n: number of items

params.name: path
params.description: Optional dot-notation path to the array within the JSON object (e.g. "data.items")

params.name: field
params.description: Field to operate on (for sort_by, group_by, count_by, uniq_by, filter)

params.name: input
params.description: The JSON containing an array (or an object with an array at `path`) — a JSON string, or the value itself.

tools.name: json_to_csv
tools.description: Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV format. Automatically detects columns from all object keys. Handles quoting and escaping per RFC 4180.

params.name: input
params.description: The array of objects to convert — a JSON string, or the array itself.

tools.name: case_convert
tools.description: Convert a string between naming conventions: camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, dot.case, Title Case. Essential for code generation and refactoring.

tools.name: sort_lines
tools.description: Sort, deduplicate, reverse, or filter lines of text. Useful for cleaning import lists, dependencies, log files, and config entries.

params.name: trim
params.description: Trim whitespace from each line (default: true)

params.name: filter
params.description: For "filter": keep lines containing this substring (case-insensitive)

tools.name: number_base_convert
tools.description: Convert numbers between bases: decimal, binary, octal, hexadecimal, or any base 2–36. Auto-detects 0x, 0b, 0o prefixes.

params.name: to_base
params.description: Target base 2–36 (omit to get all common bases)

tools.name: validate_url
tools.description: Parse and validate a URL. Returns decomposed components: protocol, hostname, port, path, query parameters, hash, and origin.

tools.name: check_contrast_ratio
tools.description: Calculate WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two colors. Returns ratio and compliance for AA/AAA normal and large text.

tools.name: html_to_markdown
tools.description: Convert HTML to clean Markdown. Strips scripts, styles, nav, ads, and comments. Converts headings, lists, links, images, code blocks. Ideal for preparing web content as LLM context.

params.name: strip_links
params.description: Strip link URLs, keep text only (default: false)

tools.name: cron_parse
tools.description: Parse a cron expression into a human-readable schedule description. Supports standard 5-field cron (minute hour day month weekday).

tools.name: cron_validator
tools.description: Validate a 5-field cron expression, explain the schedule, and preview the next execution times. Use this to debug cron jobs before they reach production. Returns parsed fields, a human-readable description, and upcoming ISO timestamps.

params.name: next_runs_count
params.description: How many upcoming runs to return (1-50, default: 10)

tools.name: calculate_readability
tools.description: Calculate readability scores: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Coleman-Liau Index, and Automated Readability Index. Useful for evaluating LLM output quality.

tools.name: normalize_whitespace
tools.description: Normalize whitespace: trim trailing spaces, collapse blank lines, normalize line endings (LF/CRLF), convert tabs to spaces. Useful for cleaning code, configs, and text before processing.

params.name: trim_lines
params.description: Trim trailing whitespace from each line (default: true)

params.name: tab_to_spaces
params.description: Convert tabs to N spaces (omit to keep tabs)

params.name: collapse_blanks
params.description: Collapse 3+ consecutive blank lines to 2 (default: true)

tools.name: embedding_similarity
tools.description: Compute text similarity using local algorithms (Bag of Words, TF-IDF, Character N-grams). No API key needed — runs entirely in-process. NOT real embeddings: for true semantic similarity with vector embeddings, use run_semantic_tests with mode="embeddings" and your OpenAI API key. Supports single pair or batch mode with pipe-separated pairs. Useful for RAG retrieval testing, semantic search evaluation, and text deduplication.

params.name: batch
params.description: Batch mode: array of { text_a, text_b } pairs. Overrides text_a/text_b if provided.

params.name: methods
params.description: Algorithms to use (default: all three). Options: "bow", "tfidf", "ngram"

tools.name: llm_format_check
tools.description: Validate that an LLM output matches an expected format: JSON, Markdown, code block, bullet list, numbered list, table, YAML, XML, or custom regex. Essential for structured output testing.

params.name: regex_pattern
params.description: Custom regex pattern (only when expected_format is "regex")

tools.name: hallucination_check
tools.description: Word-overlap based hallucination check: verifies if an LLM answer's words and numbers appear in the provided source/context. Fast, deterministic, no API key needed. Limitations: not semantic — does not understand synonyms or paraphrases. For true semantic grounding, use run_semantic_tests with embedding mode. Essential for quick RAG accuracy testing.

params.name: strict
params.description: If true, every sentence in the answer must be supported (default: false)

params.name: context
params.description: The source/reference text that should ground the answer

tools.name: prompt_injection_scan
tools.description: Scan user input or prompts for common prompt injection patterns. Detects system prompt overrides, jailbreak attempts, role manipulation, encoding tricks, delimiter attacks, template/interpolation injection ({{...}}, ${...}), and context-exfiltration attempts ("repeat everything above").

params.name: input
params.description: The user input or prompt to scan for injection patterns

tools.name: token_budget_calculator
tools.description: Plan token allocation across system prompt, user input, context/RAG chunks, and expected output. Warns if budget exceeds model context window. Supports 25+ models.

params.name: user_input
params.description: Actual user input text (will estimate tokens)

params.name: system_prompt
params.description: Actual system prompt text (will estimate tokens)

params.name: context_tokens
params.description: Token count for RAG context / documents

tools.name: consistency_check
tools.description: Compare multiple LLM responses to the same prompt and detect inconsistencies using Jaccard word-overlap similarity and fact drift (number comparison). Fast, deterministic, no API key needed. Limitations: relies on surface-level word matching — "Paris is the capital of France" vs "Paris is the French capital" may score low despite semantic equivalence. For true semantic consistency, use run_semantic_tests with embedding mode. Essential for determinism testing.

params.name: responses
params.description: Array of 2+ LLM responses to compare (same prompt, different runs)

params.name: check_facts
params.description: Check for contradictory numbers/facts across responses (default: true)

tools.name: llm_json_schema_check
tools.description: Validate that an LLM JSON output matches a JSON Schema definition. Tests required fields, types, enums, nested objects, and arrays. Critical for function-calling and structured output testing.

params.name: output
params.description: The LLM JSON output (raw string, will be parsed)

params.name: schema
params.description: JSON Schema (draft-07 subset) to validate against

tools.name: latency_benchmark
tools.description: Measure response time of one or more HTTP endpoints (GET/POST). Runs N iterations and returns min/max/avg/p95 latency. Useful for API and MCP server benchmarking.

params.name: endpoints
params.description: Endpoints to benchmark. Accepts a single URL string, an array of URL strings, or an array of {url, method?, body?, headers?, label?} objects.

params.name: iterations
params.description: Number of iterations per endpoint (default: 3, max: 10)

tools.name: response_quality_score
tools.description: Score an LLM response on multiple quality dimensions: relevance, completeness, clarity, conciseness, formatting. Returns a weighted 0-100 score with detailed breakdown.

params.name: max_length
params.description: Ideal max character length (penalize if exceeded)

params.name: expected_keywords
params.description: Keywords that should appear in a good answer

tools.name: rag_relevance_rank
tools.description: Rank an array of text chunks by relevance to a query using TF-IDF scoring. Simulates retrieval ranking for RAG testing without needing embeddings or an API.

params.name: chunks
params.description: Array of text chunks to rank

tools.name: toxicity_scan
tools.description: Scan text for toxic language, bias indicators, profanity, and harmful content categories. Returns risk scores per category. Useful for LLM safety guardrail testing.

tools.name: guardrail_test
tools.description: Test an LLM response against a set of guardrail rules: must-include, must-not-include, max length, required format, language, forbidden patterns, and custom regex. Returns pass/fail per rule.

params.name: rules
params.description: Array of guardrail rules to check

tools.name: function_call_validate
tools.description: Validate an LLM function call / tool_use output: check that function name is in allowed list, arguments match expected schema, no extra/missing args. For OpenAI function calling & MCP tool_use testing.

params.name: function_call
params.description: The function call object from LLM (e.g. { "name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city":"Paris"} })

tools.name: conversation_analyze
tools.description: Analyze a multi-turn conversation for context retention, topic drift, instruction following, and repetition. Accepts messages array [{role, content}]. Essential for chatbot QA.

tools.name: mcp_schema_lint
tools.description: Lint an MCP tool definition for best practices: naming conventions, description quality, schema completeness, required fields consistency, description length. Returns actionable warnings.

params.name: tool_definition
params.description: MCP tool definition object with name, description, inputSchema

tools.name: cot_analyzer
tools.description: Analyze a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) or reasoning trace from an LLM. Detects step count, logical flow, conclusion presence, backtracking, and estimates reasoning depth. Useful for o1/o3/DeepSeek-R1 evaluation.

params.name: reasoning
params.description: The CoT / reasoning trace text (e.g. from <think> tags or step-by-step output)

params.name: expected_conclusion
params.description: Expected final answer to check against (optional)

tools.name: ab_test_report
tools.description: Generate an A/B test report comparing two prompts or model configurations. Accepts arrays of scores and returns statistical comparison: mean, median, std deviation, winner, and improvement percentage.

params.name: variant_a
params.description: First variant configuration with name and score array

params.name: variant_b
params.description: Second variant configuration with name and score array

tools.name: context_window_check
tools.description: Given an array of message objects [{role, content}], estimate total token usage and check if it fits in the target model's context window. Warns about truncation risk.

tools.name: vector_similarity
tools.description: Compute similarity/distance between two float vectors: cosine similarity, dot product, Euclidean and Manhattan distance. Essential for vector DB relevance scoring, embedding evaluation, and nearest-neighbor testing.

params.name: vector_a
params.description: First vector as array of floats

params.name: vector_b
params.description: Second vector as array of floats

tools.name: normalize_vector
tools.description: L2-normalize a float vector (produce a unit vector with norm=1). Required by many vector DBs (Pinecone, Qdrant cosine). Supports batch normalization of up to 1000 vectors.

params.name: batch
params.description: Batch of vectors to normalize (overrides vector)

tools.name: vector_quantize
tools.description: Simulate int8 or int4 quantization of float32 embedding vectors. Reduces storage by 4x (int8) or 8x (int4). Returns quantized values, scale factor, and precision loss (MSE). Useful for understanding vector DB compression trade-offs.

tools.name: vector_stats
tools.description: Compute statistics for a float vector or matrix of vectors: mean, std, L2 norm, min, max, sparsity, top-K indices. Useful for debugging embedding quality and analyzing vector distributions in a vector DB.

params.name: top_k
params.description: Return indices of top K absolute values (default: 5)

params.name: matrix
params.description: Matrix of vectors (overrides vector). Returns per-vector + matrix-level stats. Required unless `vector` is given.

params.name: vector
params.description: Single vector to analyze. Required unless `matrix` is given.
